papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
papers.titleOriginal:
Synthesis and Characterization
of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate
Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive. Herein, we report a synthetic model of the NPN cofactor which is faithful to the cofactor in consisting of a di(thioamide) substituted pyridine ring. The hydride transfer reactivity of the NPN model was studied and both 1,4- and 1,2-dihydropyridinates (DHP–) of both the free ligand and the Ni complex have been isolated and studied spectroscopically. No evidence for Ni-hydride formation was observed. The UV–vis spectrum of the 1,4-DHP– Ni model complex (1H1,4) has features matching UV–vis spectra collected in biochemical studies where NaBH4 was added to the NPN-dependent enzyme, lactate racemase; whereas the spectra of 1-I and 1H1,2 do not match spectra collected from NPN cofactor reaction intermediates. Thus, the isolation and characterization of 1H1,4 reported herein provides the first direct experimental evidence assigning the reactivity observed in biochemical studies to the pyridyl C4 position of a NPN cofactor model complex.

papers.title: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.titleOriginal: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) provides resolved stellar abundances and star formation histories (SFHs) that can be used together to test models of dwarf-galaxy chemical evolution. We investigated if the non-monotonic APOGEE $ Mg / Fe -- Fe / H $ sequence can be explained by a hybrid history that combines a second gas-infall episode with a temporary increase in star formation efficiency (SFE). We selected 4933 LMC red giant branch stars from APOGEE-2 DR17. We fitted an adaptively binned median Mg sequence with the two-zone open-box code . The formal fitting objective contained only the Mg sequence. The metallicity distribution function (MDF), one-dimensional abundance distributions, SFH, present-day mass partition, star formation rate (SFR), and supernova (SN) rate were retained as posterior diagnostics. OMEGA+ The best-fitting model reproduces the Mg sequence with a root mean square (RMS) residual of 0.01 dex and also gives a close posterior match to O. It contains two delayed-tau infall episodes, with the second beginning at t_2=10.39 Gyr and with an integrated mass ratio of M_2/M_1=0.159, followed by a temporary Gaussian SFE enhancement centered at t=11.91 Gyr. The second infall is represented by a mixture of enriched and primordial gas. The model reproduces the timing of the late SFH enhancement and yields a present SFR within the adopted comparison range. A hybrid second-infall and SFE enhancement history is a plausible scenario for reproducing the observed LMC Mg median sequence. Our fit explains the LMC evolution fairly well, but the remaining small MDF, mass, and SN rate discrepancies suggest that a selection-function-aware treatment of the stellar distributions is required for a stricter comparison.

papers.title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
papers.titleOriginal:
Synthesis and Crystal
Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol
C(OH)4
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. The crystal structure of C(OH)4 was determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and corroborated by density-functional theory calculations together with Raman spectroscopy. It is composed of isolated [C(OH)4]-molecules linked by strong hydrogen bonds. Under high-pressure conditions, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids are denser than coexisting water ice phases, allowing them to segregate gravitationally and form stable reservoirs of oxidized carbon. These phases incorporate large amounts of carbon into their crystal structures as part of [CO4]4–- or [CO3]2–-building blocks. Because the amount of carbon that can be stored as CO2 in clathrates or filled-ices is significantly smaller, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids may provide a host mechanism for sequestering large carbon inventories in the icy mantles of water-rich exoplanets.

papers.title: Neutron star-companion interaction in core-collapse supernovae. Population synthesis based on detailed binary evolution models
papers.titleOriginal: Neutron star-companion interaction in core-collapse supernovae. Population synthesis based on detailed binary evolution models
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Most massive stars live in binary systems. When the first supernova in a binary occurs, the ejecta hit the companion, which may inflate as a consequence, and then interact with the newly formed compact object. The recent Type Ic supernova shows a periodic modulation in its emission, which is interpreted as evidence of such interaction. 2022jli We derive predictions for the occurrence rate and observables of supernovae exhibiting these compact object--companion interactions (CCIs). We analyzed a comprehensive state-of-the-art grid of detailed binary stellar evolution models and implemented analytic prescriptions for the expansion of the companion star following its interaction with the supernova ejecta. We then employed the newly developed population synthesis code to derive the distribution functions of the properties of the supernovae affected by CCI and their companions, where we used different explodability and neutron star birth-kick distributions. SN-ORACLE We find that periodic CCI is expected to occur in more than half of the binary systems that produce a hydrogen-poor core-collapse supernova and are not disrupted, while the occurrence rate in systems producing hydrogen-rich supernovae is small. We found broad period ranges, peaking around 20-50 with the interaction lasting for 0.5-10 , , and . The inflation of the companion also increases their luminosity and brightness, increasing their detectability with current instruments. For , our best-fitting models predict a J-band magnitude of 21-23 for up to sim10 We identified specific binary evolution models that reproduce the observed period of the light curve undulations of 2022jli 2015ap 2022esa 2022jli We find that up to sim27% of H-poor supernovae could show periodicity in their light curves, while only a few such events have been identified so far. Our results may help identify periodic CCI features in future and archival supernova observations.

papers.abstract: We report the first measurement of the semileptonic decay $D^+_s \rightarrow K^*(892)^0μ^+ν_μ$ and an improved measurement of the decay $D^+_s \rightarrow K^*(892)^0 e^+ν_{e}$ using a sample of $7.33~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ annihilation data collected at center-of-mass energies between 4.128 to 4.226~GeV with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider. We measure the branching fractions to be $\mathcal B({D^+_s\rightarrow K^*(892)^0 μ^+ν_μ})=(2.07\pm0.22_{\rm stat}\pm0.10_{\rm syst})\times10^{-3}$ and $\mathcal B({D^+_s\rightarrow K^*(892)^0 e^+ν_{e}})=(2.14\pm0.18_{\rm stat}\pm0.10_{\rm syst})\times10^{-3}$. Based on a simultaneous study of the dynamics in two semileptonic decays, the hadronic form factor parameters in the $D^+_s\rightarrow K^{*}(892)^0$ transition are determined to be $r_{V} = V(0)/A_1(0) = 1.63 \pm 0.14_{\rm stat} \pm 0.08_{\rm syst}$, $r_{2} = A_2(0)/A_1(0) = 0.60 \pm 0.13_{\rm stat} \pm 0.06_{\rm syst}$, and $A_1(0)=0.56 \pm 0.02_{\rm stat} \pm 0.01_{\rm syst}$, where $V(0)$ is the vector form factor and $A_{1,2}(0)$ are the axial-vector form factors evaluated at $q^2=0$. The precision of $r_V$ and $r_2$ is improved by twofold and $A_1(0)$ is measured for the first time. We also report the first model-independent measurements of the differential decay rates and the lepton forward-backward asymmetries for $D^+_s\rightarrow K^{*}(892)^0\ell^+ν_{\ell}$ decays. Based on these measurements, we perform a test of lepton flavor universality in full and separate $q^2$ intervals with $D^+_s\rightarrow K^{*}(892)^0\ell^+ν_{\ell}$ decays. No violation is found within uncertainties. Our results present for the first time a complete study of the dynamics in the $D_s^+\rightarrow K^*(892)^0$ transition, and provide stringent tests of various non-perturbative theoretical calculations.

papers.title: HCN detection in the Kreutz sungrazing comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS) shortly before its disruption
papers.titleOriginal: HCN detection in the Kreutz sungrazing comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS) shortly before its disruption
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Kreutz sungrazing comets are characterised by extremely small perihelion distances (q < 3.45 , R_⊙). These objects are of particular interest because their intense activity and fragmentation can expose material from deeper within the nucleus, providing unique access to their bulk chemical composition, rather than just their surface layers. The discovery of C/2026 A1 (MAPS) three months before its perihelion has offered a rare opportunity to investigate the composition and activity of a Kreutz sungrazing comet. We present the first millimetre wavelength study of this type of comet. We observed C/2026 A1 (MAPS) with the IRAM 30-m telescope from 1 to 3 April 2026 at heliocentric distances of r_h = 0.10--0.23,au. This time span covered the three days preceding its perihelion and full disintegration. We analysed the molecular emissions using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative transfer models to derive molecular production rates. We report the first HCN detection in a Kreutz sungrazer through its (3--2) transition at 265.886,GHz, enabling us to characterise the variability of its activity. We witnessed two outbursts, on 1 to 3 April. The second, occurring a day before the disintegration of C/2026 A1 (MAPS), led to the release of 0.4% to 1.2% of the total cometary mass, thereby suggesting a pre-disruption prior to entering the Roche limit region. We also obtained upper limits for HNC, CS, H_2CO, CO, OCS, and CH_3OH.

papers.title: DUETS: Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
papers.titleOriginal: DUETS: Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Red giants displaying solar-like oscillations allow precise model-dependent stellar properties to be derived. Asteroseismic binaries (ABs), which are gravitationally bound systems where both stars show detectable oscillations, can provide independent constraints on the interior of two coeval stars, allowing us to model them jointly and potentially obtain constraints unavailable from either star individually. This makes ABs potential laboratories for calibrating uncertain aspects of stellar evolution theory. In this context, AB candidates (ABCs) are systems showing two oscillators, which are as of yet not confirmed as gravitationally bound. The relatively coarse spatial resolution of the mission can blend unrelated oscillators into the same light curve, and past studies have found a high incidence of chance alignments in ABCs due to this. We aim to confirm ABCs and other red giant binary candidates, as well as demonstrate the advantages of AB modelling inference in constraining stellar parameters. We obtained high-resolution spectroscopic indicators of binarity for a sample of 60 oscillating red giants that have photometric (33 stars) and/or asteroseismic (38) indications of binarity. We confirm 12 of our 60 targets as spectroscopic binaries, 8 of which are ABs as well. Cross-matching with Gaia DR3 and APOGEE DR17, we identify a further 9 likely binaries, at least 6 of which are also ABCs. We then investigated the impact of simultaneously modelling the individual oscillation modes of both oscillators of an AB. We inferred stellar properties for: one binary of extragalactic origin containing one detectable red-giant-branch (RGB) oscillator; one AB with RGB oscillators; and two ABCs with RGB oscillators. We find that the mode frequencies of the two ABCs and the confirmed AB are well described with a coeval modelling of the stellar components. We demonstrate that the simultaneous modelling of ABs with two RGB stars can be used to infer the stellar helium content down to 3% precision, compared to 5% when using only the brightest star. Finally, the metal-poor binary KIC,2971380 hints at a need to correct the ν_̊m max scaling relation, supporting recent studies of extremely metal-poor oscillators. Kepler

papers.title: X-shooter DESI Lens Program: Sample characterization
papers.titleOriginal: X-shooter DESI Lens Program: Sample characterization
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Large imaging surveys in cosmology are detecting orders of magnitude more lens systems than previously known. This unprecedented dataset will provide robust constraints on cosmology and galaxy-evolution models. However, a careful, preliminary characterization of the lens and source samples is required. In this work, we report on a VLT/X-shooter observation program of 67 lens systems to characterize their spectroscopic redshift distribution. These systems were previously detected in the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Legacy Imaging Surveys with a deep residual neural network. We reduced the spectra and estimated redshifts from absorption and emission features, with quality flags based on feature robustness. We measured redshifts for 58 lenses and 57 sources. We identify two sources with indications of outflow in the shape of the emission lines and seven sources with rotating disks in O II or Hα. We find that the lens and source redshift success rates are independent of color and that source redshifts are independent of object magnitudes. In contrast, lens redshifts are mostly determined from absorption features, and their distribution is biased toward objects brighter than z_ <20. AB

papers.title: Minimum observations for accurate exoplanetary mass estimation with radial velocity analysis ( MINERVA )
papers.titleOriginal: Minimum observations for accurate exoplanetary mass estimation with radial velocity analysis ( MINERVA )
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Precise planetary mass measurements are essential for constraining the internal structure and envelope properties of exoplanets. For current and future characterisation programs, such data are crucial to break key degeneracies in atmospheric retrievals. Estimating the observational effort needed to reach the desired mass precision is therefore fundamental for the optimisation of current and future radial velocity (RV) surveys. We present , a tool designed to estimate the required number of RV observations to measure transiting planet masses to a given precision and that therefore provides a robust scheduling framework for large-scale samples. MINERVA MINERVA simulates realistic RV time series for targets orbiting FGKM-type stars. Recognising that signal recovery heavily depends on temporal sampling, the code explicitly ingests real-world observational timestamps to rigorously account for weather interruptions and seasonal visibility gaps. To model stellar activity, the pipeline draws ages from local neighbourhood distributions, uses empirical calibrations to derive rotation and magnetic activity levels, and translates these into time-varying RV signals. During development, we also derived a new empirical calibration between chromospheric activity and RV dispersion for K-type stars using Global Architecture of Planetary Systems (GAPS) and Mass Survey (ArMS) data. Ariel We successfully validated on targets with known planetary masses, which yielded required observational efforts highly consistent literature values. To demonstrate its capabilities on statistically significant samples, we applied the code to a sub-sample of the Mission Candidate Sample. Adopting HARPS-N/TNG as the reference instrument, we estimated the observing nights necessary to achieve a 30% planetary mass precision and thus obtained an optimised observational roadmap for atmospheric characterisation. MINERVA Ariel Beyond observing proposal preparation, 's probabilistic and flexible architecture allows for the optimisation of ongoing RV campaigns, the evaluation of undersampling risks in active stars, and the dynamic guidance of population-wide characterisation strategies. papers.title: Mechanisms of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
papers.titleOriginal:
Mechanisms
of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index
Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Ammonia is a vital compound for the future, with significant potential in energy applications, such as hydrogen-powered vehicles, and in agriculture as a key ingredient in fertilizers essential for food production. Traditionally, ammonia has been synthesized via the Haber-Bosch process using an iron catalyst, which requires high temperatures (400 to 500 °C) and pressures (about 200 atm), leading to a substantial carbon footprint and energy costs. Ruthenium is a promising alternative catalyst due to its higher intrinsic catalytic activity, allowing for ammonia synthesis under milder conditions. This paper presents a detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) study of the elementary steps involved in ammonia production across five distinct facets: Ru(0001), Ru(10–10), Ru(11–20), Ru(11–21), and Ru(10–11). Using vibrational frequency analysis, we applied zero-point energy (ZPE), enthalpic, and entropic corrections at 80 °C. We also examined the competition with the hydrogen evolution reaction. Ultimately, we find that the step-edge coordination of the Ru(11–21) surface offers the most favorable thermodynamic pathway for NH3 formation and the most efficient catalytic performance. Nudged elastic band calculations on Ru(11–21) show that hydrogenation mediated by coadsorbed water has low barriers and that NH3 desorption is the most demanding step. Further, the Ru(11–21) surface favors water dissociation, while H2 evolution on the clean surface is uphill by 0.5 eV in free energy.

papers.title: Entropy of non-Abelian anyons from slow quasiparticle dynamics in quantum Hall interferometers
papers.titleOriginal: Entropy of non-Abelian anyons from slow quasiparticle dynamics in quantum Hall interferometers
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian anyons emerging in fractional quantum Hall states carry a characteristic entropy, $ΔS = k_B \log d$, where $d$ is the anyon's quantum dimension. This $\mathcal{O}(1)$ entropy can, in principle, be extracted from charge measurements of an antidot via Maxwell relations. However, equilibrium charge measurements in fractional antidots have proven to be challenging with conventional charge detectors. Here, we propose a scheme based on an antidot embedded in an interferometer, in which the charge can be inferred from the recently observed time-dependent switching of the interference phase. Performing such non-local charge measurements at equilibrium, the characteristic $\mathcal{O}(1)$ entropy of non-Abelian anyons (e.g., $d = \sqrt{2}$ for the $ν= 5/2$ state) can be extracted for intermediate temperatures, which exceed the level spacing of the interferometer edge, but are much smaller than the level spacing of the antidot.

papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: We report a measurement of the charged-current coherent pion production cross section on argon using the MicroBooNE liquid argon time projection chamber exposed to the Booster Neutrino Beam at Fermilab. The measurement uses the MicroBooNE data set corresponding to 1.26 × 10 21 protons on target with a mean neutrino energy of 0.8 ~GeV. The flux-averaged cross section is measured to be ( 9.1 ± 1.2 stat ± 1.2 syst ) × 10 − 40 cm 2 / Ar . This result represents the first measurement of charged-current coherent pion production on argon at sub-GeV neutrino energies. Due to its clean two-body kinematics, where the neutrino interacts coherently with the entire nucleus producing a forward muon and pion with no nuclear breakup, this process provides a useful tool for constraining neutrino flux uncertainties in current and future oscillation experiments such as DUNE.

papers.title: Statistical characterization of valley coupling in Si/SiGe quantum dots via g -factor measurements near a valley vortex
papers.titleOriginal:
Statistical characterization of valley coupling in Si/SiGe quantum dots via
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <mml:mi>g</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    -factor measurements near a valley vortex
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: The presence of low-energy valley excitations in Si/SiGe heterostructures often causes spin qubits to fail. It is therefore important to develop robust protocols for characterizing the valley coupling. Here, we show that realistically sized samplings of valley energy distributions tend to dramatically overestimate the average valley coupling. But we find that knowledge of the valley phase, in addition to the valley splitting, can significantly improve our estimates. Motivated by this understanding, we propose a novel method to probe the valley phase landscape across the quantum well using simple g-factor measurements. An important calibration step in this procedure is to measure g in a loop enclosing a valley vortex, where the valley phase winds by 2 π around a zero of the valley splitting. This proposal establishes an important new tool for probing spin qubits, and it can be implemented in current experiments.

papers.title: Deriving physical parameters of unresolved star clusters. X. Size evolution of young star clusters in the M31 disc
papers.titleOriginal: Deriving physical parameters of unresolved star clusters. X. Size evolution of young star clusters in the M31 disc
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Star cluster structural properties and their correlations with other cluster parameters (age, mass, galactocentric distance) provide key constraints on cluster formation and dynamical evolution within star-forming galactic discs. In the tenth paper of this series, we analysed structural parameters of 1918 young star clusters (up to 800,Myr) in the disc of M,31 . We aim to examine the structural evolution of disc clusters and determine how their sizes correlate with physical and spatial properties. Our goal is to improve the understanding of cluster formation and evolution in spiral galaxy discs. M,31 We use the disc cluster parameter catalogue based on photometric measurements of the Panchromatic Andromeda Treasury survey data. We perform statistical analysis to determine how cluster structural parameters relate to their physical characteristics and location within the disc. M,31 Hubble Young clusters in the disc of are compact (R_ M,31 50 and expand rapidly during the first ∼20,Myr, more than doubling in size. At older ages, M,31 clusters follow a weak age--radius relation (R_ 50 ∝ t^ 0.12 ). We find no significant correlation between cluster size and galactocentric distance, indicating that internal processes dominate their early evolution, with minimal impact from the galactic tidal field. Our results suggest that stellar-evolution-driven mass loss and internal dynamical interactions are likely drivers of early cluster structural evolution in the disc. A shallow mass–radius relation emerges for clusters older than 100,Myr (R_ M,31 50 ∝ M^ 0.18 ), while the trend for younger clusters remains uncertain. The diversity of mass–radius relations observed in nearby spiral galaxies, both within and beyond the Local Group, highlights the need for further theoretical work on cluster formation and evolution.

papers.title: White dwarf pollution in wide binaries. I. the effects of stellar evolution
papers.titleOriginal: White dwarf pollution in wide binaries. I. the effects of stellar evolution
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Atmospheric pollution in white dwarfs is interpreted as evidence for the accretion of rocky material from remnant planetary systems. Wide binary companions can influence the delivery of planetary material onto white dwarfs, making it essential to understand the interplay between stellar evolution and binary perturbations. We investigate how uncertainties in stellar mass-loss histories affect the dynamical evolution of remnant planetary systems in wide binaries, and assess their relative importance compared with binary perturbations in driving the accretion of rocky material onto white dwarfs. We performed N-body simulations incorporating time-dependent stellar parameters interpolated from evolutionary tracks and tidal interactions, following the dynamical evolution up to the white dwarf stage. We explored two stellar-evolution models with distinct mass-loss histories for wide binary systems hosting a Jupiter-mass planet and a planetesimal disc, spanning a range of binary architectures. REBOUND MESA The adopted stellar-evolution model has only a minor effect on the survival of the planet, mainly affecting the timing and efficiency of planetesimal delivery during the white dwarf stage. Instead, the architecture of the binary primarily controls the pollution outcome: wider binaries produce the highest rates of accretion onto the white dwarf, consistent with the observed prevalence of polluted white dwarfs in wide binaries. Moreover, planetesimal reservoirs remain long-lived, with survival times increasing with binary separation, enabling gigayear-long metal pollution. Our results suggest that the architecture of wide binaries, rather than uncertainties in stellar evolution, is the dominant factor controlling the dynamical delivery of rocky material onto white dwarfs.

papers.abstract: Assessing whether disc evolution is driven by viscosity or magneto hydro-dynamic (MHD) winds is crucial to determine the conditions in which planets form. The rich statistical information encoded in the nearby star-forming regions provides an excellent opportunity to probe disc evolution. In this paper, we apply the Bayesian inference tool , which is designed to fully exploit the statistical properties of disc populations and infer initial conditions and model parameters, to the Lupus disc population. We consider the observed distribution of stellar mass, M_⋆, disc mass, M (obtained from continuum flux), mass accretion rate, . We constrain all parameters for both the viscous model, which includes dispersal driven by internal photoevaporation, and the MHD winds model, with unprecedented precision. The inferred initial conditions suggest that positive correlations between initial disc properties, such as mass, M_0, and truncation radius, R_0, with the stellar mass, M_⋆, must be already present in the population before the disc phase. According to both models, the typical R_0 for a disc around a 0.3 DEMOS and CO disc size, R_ 90%, CO M _⊙ star is 3-5 au, with a strong dependence on stellar mass of ∼ 2 and ∼ 1 for the viscous-photo-evaporative and MHD winds models, respectively. We infer values for the angular momentum transport parameter α (or α_ in both models, for discs around 0.3 of 3-4 10^ -4 M _⊙ stars, and an approximately quadratic dependence on M_⋆. For the viscous-photo-evaporative model, we infer a typical wind mass-loss rate of dot M _ ∼ 10^ w -9 M_⊙ yr -1 $ for a disc around a 0.3 M _⊙ star, and a steep correlation with M_⋆ with an exponent $∼ 2.5. The inferred mean age of the Lupus population differs between models, with łangle t̊angle = 1.6 Myr for the MHD winds model and łangle t̊angle = 0.9 Myr for the viscous-photo-evaporative framework. Despite indicating a slight preference for the viscous-photo-evaporative framework, the Bayesian evidence computed with shows that both models reproduce the data with comparable accuracy and does not allow either scenario to be ruled out. papers.title: Self-Induced Spin Glass in Triangular-Lattice MnNCN Stabilized by High-Pressure Synthesis
papers.titleOriginal:
Self-Induced Spin Glass
in Triangular-Lattice MnNCN
Stabilized by High-Pressure Synthesis
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract The realization of spin glasses in the absence of structural disorder remains an enduring challenge in condensed matter physics and solid-state chemistry. Geometrical frustration provides a route to disordered magnetism in long-range ordered crystals, yet canonical self-induced spin glass (SISG) beyond ultrapure rare-earth elements remains experimentally elusive. Here, we realize a metastable transition-metal SISG phase in MnNCN (R3̅m) via high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis, stabilizing a nonequilibrium state with enhanced magnetic competition. Magnetic measurements establish canonical spin-glass behavior, featuring a freezing temperature of 38.15 K and characteristic slowing-down dynamics, alongside a high coercivity of 1838 Oe. First-principles calculations reveal this SISG behavior is inherently rooted in the frustrated Mn triangular lattice. Mapping the energetic hierarchy uncovers strong competition among distinct antiferromagnetic superexchange pathways. Crucially, high-pressure-driven anisotropic lattice compression alters the Mn-ligand orbital overlap, significantly amplifying the intralayer coupling within the ab triangular planes. This chemical–mechanical modulation intensifies the competition between intralayer and dominant interlayer couplings, producing a strongly frustrated three-dimensional magnetic network. Energy evaluations verify a profound near-degeneracy among these competing states. Rapid quenching kinetically preserves this structurally ordered metastable phase, generating the complex energy landscape characteristic of a spin glass. Electronic-structure analyses further identify the Mn–N–C–N–Mn superexchange pathway mediated by covalent [N═C═N]2– ligands as the origin of magnetic coupling, yielding an intrinsic phase robustness surpassing fragile rare-earth SISGs. Magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) calculations suggest that the high coercivity mainly arises from extrinsic spin pinning associated with the nanograined microstructure, contributing to macroscopic anti-interference. Ultimately, the creation of the MnNCN SISG and the elucidation of its magnetic competition extend the SISG paradigm to transition-metal compounds, establishing HPHT synthesis as a targeted methodology for tailoring complex magnetism.

papers.title: Emergent chaotic-like dynamics in interacting liquid crystal directrons
papers.titleOriginal: Emergent chaotic-like dynamics in interacting liquid crystal directrons
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: Biological systems often operate at the boundary between order and chaos, where collective interactions give rise to robust, adaptive, and dynamically diverse behaviours. Reproducing such interaction-driven transitions in synthetic active matter remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we show that directrons - electric field-induced propagating director deformations in achiral nematic liquid crystals - can exhibit multiple coexisting motility states and interaction-driven switching between them under nominally uniform, weak planar surface anchoring. Unlike conventional active particles, directrons are dynamically deformable liquid-crystal structures whose motility states are coupled to their internal director configuration. Weak surface anchoring creates an electric-field-tunable energy landscape in which directrons exhibit multiple coexisting configurations with different propagation directions and degrees of LC deformation. Interactions between directrons induce stochastic transitions between these configurations. Increasing the electric field enhances the persistence of higher-deformation configurations through flexoelectric stabilization and increases the interaction frequency, thereby promoting state-switching events, stochastic trajectory reorientation, dynamic assembly formation, and spontaneous fission of highly distorted directrons. Above a crossover voltage, the system transitions from directed propagation to strongly fluctuating interaction-dominated regime characterized by enhanced trajectory divergence and loss of directional predictability. A non-equilibrium kinetic analysis and a minimal interaction model reveal that the transition occurs when internal-state persistence and interaction frequency become comparable, yielding a unified phase diagram for the directed-to-disordered transition. Overall, our results establish directron ensembles as a minimal electrically tunable active-matter platform for investigating interaction-driven dynamical disorder arising from coupled internal-state dynamics.

papers.title: Polar-structure galaxies beyond the local Universe: First results from Euclid
papers.titleOriginal: Polar-structure galaxies beyond the local Universe: First results from Euclid
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Galaxies hosting strongly misaligned stellar and gas structures offer a direct window into external accretion and the buildup of angular momentum through multiple spin components. Such polar-structure systems are intrinsically rare and have been identified almost entirely at low redshift so far. The Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) with its uniform space-based Visible Instrument imaging provides an unprecedented opportunity to locate these objects over wide areas and at much greater distances. We present the first visual search for polar-structure galaxy (PSG) candidates in Euclid Visible Instrument data, spanning approximately 10% of the Q1 survey footprint. This search yields the largest high-redshift PSG candidate sample assembled to date, including roughly 100 high-confidence systems with over 50 at z ≳ 0.3, along with additional populations of face-on rings and polar tidal structures. Robust candidates are detected out to redshifts of z demonstrating that polar structures can be identified well beyond the local Universe. Although the present sample is not yet sufficient for quantitative occurrence rate or evolutionary measurements, it enables initial classification and basic structural characterization of PSGs at intermediate redshift. These results lay the groundwork for future statistical studies with forthcoming Euclid data releases and illustrate Euclid’s power for rare-object science across cosmic time.

papers.title: High-quality pig pan-genome resources illuminate centromere evolution and enhance genotype–phenotype mapping
papers.titleOriginal: High-quality pig pan-genome resources illuminate centromere evolution and enhance genotype–phenotype mapping
papers.subject: Biology
papers.abstract: Pigs are important agricultural resources and valuable biomedical models, necessitating a high-quality pan-genome to comprehensively capture genomic diversity. Here we present an extensive genomic and phenotypic resource comprising 3 telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genomes and 16 high-quality assemblies. This resource enables the construction of the pig pan-transcriptome and pan-metabolome, thereby enhancing genotype-phenotype mapping. Using 12 Y-chromosome assemblies, we resolved centromere repositioning at basepair resolution, establishing centromeres as unique evolutionary markers. Reconstruction of centromeric three-dimensional genomic architecture revealed their role as structural scaffolds that concentrate chromatin interactions. We identified eEF1A1, a transcriptionally active gene consistently located near chromosome 1 centromeres, as a candidate hotspot for karyotype variation. From a pan-structural variation map, we pinpointed AKR1B1 as a key gene underlying hypoxia adaptation. Moreover, a graph-based pan-genome built from T2T genomes improved heritability capture. Together, this work provides a foundation for studies of centromere evolution, adaptive genetics and precision breeding.

papers.title: Proton-Coupled Electrostatic Regulation of Anion Electrosorption in Electric Double Layers
papers.titleOriginal:
Proton-Coupled Electrostatic
Regulation of Anion Electrosorption
in Electric Double Layers
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Electric double layers underpin electrochemical energy storage and modulate interfacial reactivity through the organization of ions and solvent molecules. However, regulating anion accumulation at compact aqueous interfaces while limiting parasitic water reactions remains challenging. Here, anodic polarization reconstructs oxygen-deficient TiO2–x into a depth-graded architecture comprising a rutile interior, a disordered interlayer, and a thin crystalline anatase surface. This architecture establishes an internal electric field that promotes subsurface proton accumulation, creating a responsive charge distribution that regulates anion electrosorption and moderates lateral anion interactions. The thin crystalline surface complements this electrostatic regulation by extending the accessible anodic operating range, combining enhanced interfacial charge storage with high-voltage aqueous operation. Symmetric aqueous supercapacitors sustain cycling over 3.0 V in neutral Na2SO4 for 45,000 cycles and over 2.7 V in natural seawater. These findings identify subsurface ionic chemistry as a design variable for regulating anion electrosorption at aqueous oxide interfaces.

papers.title: Correlative Multidimensional Tracking and Modeling Reveals Mechanical Regulation of Nanoparticle Endocytosis
papers.titleOriginal:
Correlative Multidimensional
Tracking and Modeling
Reveals Mechanical Regulation of Nanoparticle Endocytosis
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Understanding nanoparticle–membrane interactions during endocytosis is critical for advancing nanomedicine. However, a comprehensive understanding of its dynamic complexity remains elusive, largely due to limitations in often oversimplified theoretical models and experimental challenges in correlating nanoparticle conformations and protein assemblies. To bridge this persistent theoretical–experimental divide, we developed an integrated approach combining multidimensional single-particle tracking with theoretical modeling for understanding clathrin-mediated endocytosis of rod-shaped nanoparticle cargos in live cells. Real-time tracking reveals a characteristic seesaw-like rotational motion of nanocargos that is temporally correlated with clathrin and dynamin recruitment, enabling the endocytic process to be classified into six distinct stages. Theoretical modeling, informed by these experimental observations, identifies orientation-dependent energy preferences arising from the interplay between membrane-associated effects and clathrin lattice elasticity, yielding orientation trends consistent with experimental observations. By focusing on this core structural framework, our work establishes a quantitative foundation for understanding how geometric and mechanical interactions govern the nanoparticle internalization. This correlative experimental and theoretical work is exemplary of the renewed efforts to establish closer connections between experimental evidence and theoretical modeling with higher biological complexity.

papers.titleOriginal: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines

papers.abstract: Abstract Spin state offers a fundamental yet underexplored handle for controlling stereoselectivity in transition-metal catalysis. Here we show that metal-centered spin-state switching, within an invariant weak-field bipyridine framework, promotes E/Z divergence in allylic substitution, enabling access to geometrically defined allylamines from common precursors. High-spin Ni catalysts selectively afford E-allylamines, whereas low-spin Pd catalysts deliver the corresponding Z-isomers. Broad metal studies with Fe, Rh and Ir systems further support the association between metal-centered spin state and alkene geometry. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory (DFT) analyses reveal the origin of this stereodivergent outcome: spin-state-dependent electronic structures reshape catalyst–substrate interactions, thereby selectively stabilizing the competing E- or Z-forming transition states. The paired E/Z products enable concise syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant molecules and reveal configuration-dependent biological activities. This work establishes catalyst spin state as a design parameter for the stereodivergent control of alkene geometry.

papers.title: Hydration Shell Structure and Water-Mediated Binding of Closo -Dodecaborates Probed by Raman Hydration-Shell Spectroscopy
papers.titleOriginal: Hydration Shell Structure and Water-Mediated Binding of Closo -Dodecaborates Probed by Raman Hydration-Shell Spectroscopy
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract The binding of closo-dodecaborates, B12X122– (where X = H, Cl, Br, I), to solutes and interfaces has widely been attributed to a water-mediated (super)chaotropic effect. The role of water, however, has so far been inferred only indirectly from thermodynamic measurements. Herein, we employ Raman hydration-shell spectroscopy in the OH stretch region to investigate B12X122– in aqueous solution. Specifically, we elucidate (i) the water structure in the hydration shell, (ii) its temperature dependence, and (iii) the water release upon superchaotropic binding. The hydration-shell spectra reveal that all dodecaborates give rise to a sharp Raman band close to 3600 cm–1. This feature is strongly blue-shifted compared to bulk water and represents weakly H-bonded, “almost dangling” OH groups in the hydration shell. Heating is found to blue-shift the hydration water resonance less than the bulk water resonance. Hydration and bulk water resonances thus become more similar at high temperature. This trend reflects a progressively reduced difference in hydrogen-bonding energy upon heating between hydration and bulk water, and is opposite to that of hydrophobic hydration. Furthermore, hydration difference spectra in the presence of the nonionic polymer hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) reveal that weakly H-bonded hydration water is released from B12X122– upon superchaotropic binding, together with more strongly H-bonded hydration water from the hydration shells of both B12X122– and HPC. These findings identify weakly bound hydration water, its weak temperature dependence, and its spontaneous release upon binding as molecular hallmarks of the superchaotropic behavior of B12X122–.

papers.title: Secondary Solvation Shell Regulation for Fast-Charging Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.titleOriginal:
Secondary Solvation
Shell Regulation for Fast-Charging
Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Most electrolyte strategies in lithium metal batteries (LMBs) target the first solvation shell or solvation diversity. However, such approaches have shown limited success in enabling fast-charging, as Li+ depletion inevitably develops at polarized interfaces. Here, we identify the secondary solvation shell as a critical regulator of fast-charging stability and show that a gradient solvation structure (GSS) overcomes ion depletion-induced failure. Guided by intrinsic solvation strengths, we design a tri-solvent electrolyte comprising 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), 1,1,1-trifluoro-2,3-dimethoxypropane (TFDMP), and N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethane-sulfonamide (DMTMSA). DME and TFDMP define a stable primary solvation shell and balanced ion-pair distribution, whereas DMTMSA localizes in the secondary shell, suppressing long-range ionic clustering and maintaining interfacial ion availability. Despite similar primary-shell structures and equilibrium impedances, only the tri-solvent system preserves interfacial kinetics under depletion conditions. This architecture enables a Coulombic efficiency of 98.4% at 16 mA cm–2, a specific capacity of 162.0 mAh g–1 at 10C, and 90.4% capacity retention for 200 cycles. These findings establish a gradient solvation structure as a governing principle for fast-charging LMB electrolytes.

papers.abstract: Abstract Thiol-ene click is a powerful reaction for its high efficiency, functional-group tolerance, and operational simplicity, yet regio- and stereocontrol in radical thiol addition to internal alkenes as well as its potential use in the stereoselective synthesis of semicrystalline polymers has received much less attention. Here, we report a substrate-enabled, perfectly (>99%) regio- and diastereoselective thiol-ene click reaction of a bicyclic lactone alkene, BiL=, with diverse thiols and its application in thiol-ene photopolymerization to regio- and stereoregular polythioethers (PTEs) with excellent thermomechanical and barrier properties. Using either racemic (rac) BiL= or enantiopure (1S,5S)-BiL=, the reaction proceeds through the same highly regio- and facial-selective addition pathway to afford the preferred thioether product, with rac-BiL= forming an enantiomeric pair of diastereomers and (1S,5S)-BiL= affording a single diastereomer. This unique selectivity is translatable into regio- and diastereoselective step-growth photopolymerization between a bis(bicyclic lactone alkene), Bis-BiL=, and various dithiols, affording semicrystalline PTEs with melting temperature up to 131 °C, high thermal stability, tunable mechanical properties, melt processability, and excellent oxygen-barrier performance. The inherently available main-chain postmodification sites in the PTE structure can be readily utilized to achieve reversible or irreversible modifications of the polymer main-chain structure, further modulating material performance.

papers.title: Expanding Chemical Space Enables Data–Driven Structure–Activity Relationships in Cage Catalysis
papers.titleOriginal:
Expanding Chemical Space Enables Data–Driven
Structure–Activity Relationships in Cage Catalysis
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Data-driven approaches are increasingly popular in catalysis, supplementing and even replacing traditional strategies that relied on empirical optimization. However, their application in the field of bioinspired cage catalysis remains largely unexplored, primarily due to the limited chemical space of known catalytically active cages. As a result, mechanistic insights are often obtained using computationally intensive DFT calculations on a handful of structurally similar cages. As chemical systems grow in complexity, this approach becomes impractical. Herein, we report a framework that significantly expedites the exploration of a much wider structural landscape while offering computational insights. This is made possible by a novel in situ experimental procedure─which circumvents the traditional time-consuming process of prepare, isolate, characterize, and test─coupled with data-driven methods to identify molecular features that govern activity. Using this approach, we experimentally explore 30 unique PdnL2n cages (n = 2–4) that mediate a nitro-aldol reaction with activities spanning over 4 orders of magnitude. Using this data set, a random forest model trained on molecular descriptors was developed to predict ΔG‡ (MAE of 0.4 kcal mol–1 and R2 = 0.9). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted geometric preorganization and electrostatic interactions within the cage as key determinants of catalytic efficiency. Moreover, DFT calculations on a selection of cages further validated these insights, indicating that meaningful mechanistic understanding can be achieved at significantly reduced computational cost. We anticipate that this integrated, screening, data-driven, mechanistic strategy will provide a blueprint workflow for understanding metal–organic cage reactivity and encourage the generation of more comprehensive structural data sets, ultimately enabling the rational design of improved catalytic architectures.

papers.title: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
papers.titleOriginal:
Unraveling the Intrinsic
Interfacial Chemistry of
Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free
Model System
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) is a widely used film-forming additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes (LMAs), yet its intrinsic interfacial chemistry remains elusive because its reactions are coupled with those of solvents and Li salts in conventional electrolytes. Herein, a solvent-free, dry-processed poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolyte (PEO@Dry) is developed as a platform to isolate the interfacial reactions of FEC without interference from traditional liquid organic solvents. PEO@Dry retains the intrinsic interfacial reactivity of PEO and LiTFSI while eliminating solvent-derived interference. FEC is found to undergo a spontaneous chemical reaction with Li metal before electrochemical reduction, producing a dense LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that is subsequently reinforced by organic species derived from the electrochemical reactions. The resulting SEI exhibits a well-defined composition and robust structure, leading to an enhanced interfacial stability and electrochemical performance. Comparative research with a DME-based liquid electrolyte reveals that FEC (DME@FEC) follows distinct reaction pathways depending on its solvation state. In the solvent-free PEO@Dry system, free FEC undergoes sequential chemical and electrochemical reduction to form an inorganic-rich SEI, whereas in the liquid electrolyte, FEC participates in Li+ solvation and competes with other electrolyte components, yielding a more complex SEI. This work clarifies the interfacial mechanism of FEC and establishes a general solvent-free platform for mechanistic studies of electrolyte additives on LMAs.

papers.title: Local Characterization of Global Tensor Network Eigenstates
papers.titleOriginal: Local Characterization of Global Tensor Network Eigenstates
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: We study the conditions under which matrix product states (MPSs) or matrix product operators are exact eigenvectors of an extensive local operator such as a Hamiltonian. By suitably choosing the local operator, this covers a wide range of settings: exact eigenstates of Hamiltonians, including scar states; exact MPS trajectories for driven quantum systems; steady states of local Lindbladians; generalized symmetries of either Hamiltonians or density matrices; and many more. Our key result is that a local, fixed-size equation—namely, how a single term in the operator acts on a block of tensors—provides a necessary and sufficient condition for exact solutions. This local characterization allows us to obtain the full space of MPS solutions to all of the aforementioned problems; in particular, we exemplify the power of our results by recovering the quantum group symmetries of the XXZ model. We also discuss applications to numerical algorithms with MPSs and the generalization of our results to 2D, i.e., projected entangled pair states.
